decision: The text was drafted from the Consistency classes of a private A/B defect catalogue of one Rust change. The skill is not measured on that same change.

evidence.text: Requirement of the drafting brief for backlog item 47: record the provenance and the exclusion in each skill of the family.

reopen_if: Never for that change. Any other change, in any language, is a valid workpiece.
why: The catalogue holds the confirmed defects of that change, so an arm that loads this skill there would be reading the judges' answers, and its score would say nothing about the skill.

anchors: the searches for the review. It ships no scripts.
decision: The Rust companion ships no scripts; it names what rustc, rustdoc and clippy report and gives grep and git-diff lines for the rest.

evidence.text: Each named lint fired on the table's lines when switched on (clippy 0.1.95); the grep listed every planted pair of a test file; the diff line was run on a scratch repository.

reopen_if: A recurring review step is done by hand that the toolchain and a one-line search cannot do.
why: The mechanical part is either already a lint (casts, integer division) or needs a reader to group hits by quantity; neither is work for a bundled script.

anchors: A field that is assigned but never read gets no warning.
decision: The skill states that a field which is assigned and never read draws no dead_code warning, and sends the reviewer to list the readers by search.

evidence.text: rustc 1.95.0: a private field only initialised warns 'field is never read'; after one method assigns it the warning is gone with no reader anywhere.

reopen_if: A later rustc or clippy reports assigned-but-never-read fields by default.
why: It is the mechanism behind stored state kept for a use that does not exist, and a reader who trusts the compiler to flag unused fields will not look.

anchors: The examples show the SHAPE. The rule inside each one (a substring test, a 20 % share, half-up
decision: The code examples carry their own rule and the text says the spec's rule replaces it.

evidence.text: Carried over from the Python companion's probe result; the Rust reviewer arms did not misread the examples.

why: Same reading risk as in the Python companion: an example's rule taken as the recommended one.
